title: 01 Halde Architekten: Swiss architecture hero
strengths: A drawing only this studio would have: a building section with the 21 Dec and 21 Jun sun lines, altitude labels and level marks, drawn in the page's own red and ink
One typeface (Inter Tight) carries nav, index, body and the display line; weight and size do all the hierarchy
Small true-to-world data in the corners (47.37 N 8.54 E, Sunrise 07:38, an index of eight named projects with places and years) reads like a real office, not a template
slop_signals: Three competing centres on one screen: the index, the section drawing and the giant 'Houses that follow the sun.' line all ask to be read first
'Start a project ->' filled button next to an underlined 'Read the method' is the stock pair
The red slab fills on the drawing's floors and the diagonal hatching read slightly diagrammatic next to the precision of the rest
fixes: Let the headline own the first screen and push the index below it, or shrink the headline to a two-column width so the drawing stays the subject
Drop the second CTA or make 'Read the method' a plain text link in the index column
Give the section drawing one more level of care: wall thickness, a ground line, a figure for scale, as Heron AI's elevation does

references.what: An architectural elevation drawing is the whole hero, with frame ticks and coordinates in the corners and the headline at the bottom; its drawing carries more rendering (trees, concrete) than ours
Huge type is the layout, tiny mono labels pinned to the corners; same move as our bottom headline, with less competing around it
One line drawing, one mono caption, nothing else; shows how much quieter the first screen could be
Labels pinned to the four edges of an otherwise empty page; our corner data follows this

changed: The building section is now the one object: about 680 px tall at 1 m = 32 px across all twelve columns; the project index and the column guides are gone (the index survives as 'Work 24' and '01 of 24')

Drawn as an architect would: poché slabs, retaining walls, 1.40 m overhangs, balustrades, level marks, a 0.8 m hatched cut-earth band, dimension chains with extension lines (8.00 / 8.00 / 12.40, 1.40, 7.24), a title block with scale bar, outline figures and a 1:200 winter tree

Sun geometry computed for Flims (46.83 N): 19.7 deg on 21 Dec reaches 7.24 m in; 66.6 deg on 21 Jun stops 0.06 m short of the glass; light shown once outside (ray) and once inside (wedge); red never sets text
Headline cut to one line at 88 px, weight 500, in a band ruled off from the drawing; the red full stop stays as the sun
One action: an underlined 'Start a project' link replaces the filled button plus link
Fixes from fresh eyes: 'looking west' (was east), Zurich sunrise 07:41 (was 07:38), key at 16 px on the paper, no repeated numbers or place names

facts: Halde is one letter from Halden Private (app-screens/01) and Halden Freight (components/06); still unresolved in NAMES.md, and renaming would also change mockups/02 and mockups/08
mockups/02-laptop-desk alt text still describes the removed numbered project index

pairwise.note: Judged on the first round-4 render; later rounds only removed things (the tree, the rays in open air, a figure) and ran the earth to the frame edges.

changed: Headline moved to the top, two lines at the 95 px token (was one line at 88 px, tight to the bottom edge); the red full stop is gone
Nav reduced to the wordmark and four links: the 'Zurich and Chur, since 1998' line, the coordinates and the sunrise time are gone (the places moved into the one supporting line)

Drawing cleared to the building, its rooms and the light: dimension chains, level marks, angle arcs, the two-line key, the title block with its scale bar, the summer rays, the balustrade posts, the tree, the dashed rays in open air and one of the two figures in the lowest room are gone
The winter light is shown once per room: a pale wedge with a 1.2 px edge at 19.7 degrees, inside the room only

Drawn at 1 m = 36 px (was 32) so the section fills the frame; the cut earth is one flat tone from the cut ground to the foot of the frame, running to both frame edges (the hatched band read as a drop shadow)
One caption on the earth: 'Haus am Hang, Flims, 2025 · noon, 21 December'
